thread:
Mia: Quick heads-up — ran the Iris customer LoRA (iris-lora-v3) through an int4 quick-probe on the nightly bench. Saw a few odd numeric formatting regressions and one prompt that truncates mid-number. Full run attached below.

Devin: ack, can you drop the command + the top failing samples?

Mia: command I used:
```
./bench/run_quick_eval --model iris-lora-v3 --quant=int4 --prompts=customers/iris/smoke_prompts.json --out=/tmp/iris_int4_smoke.json --batch=8
```
Top metrics summary: pass 48/60, numeric-integrity 0.86 (baseline float16: 0.99), mean-token-len delta +7%, BLEU-ish 0.74 -> 0.72.

Mia: failing examples (redacted):
1) prompt id 12: expected "$1,234.56" -> got "$1,234." (truncated)
2) prompt id 19: expected "42.0" -> got "42 .0" (space injected)
3) prompt id 33: long table row, model produces truncated second row after 128 tokens

Devin: hmm spacing/regression like that smells like tokenizer mismatch or quantization rounding rules. Did you use the same tokenizer + merge file as baseline?

Mia: yes, same tokenizer artifacts. I re-run with `--use-tokenizer=customers/iris/tokenizer.json` and same results. Also tried bias-correction flag off/on, no change.

Arjun: could be kv-cache alignment with LoRA + int4 kernels if sequence lengths differ. Did bench include the long-context warmup?

Mia: bench warmup seq=64, test seqs include 512/1024. The truncation happens on 1024 samples.

Sara: any diffs in detokenization config? e.g., merge rules or postprocess strip?

Mia: detokenize config matches. I diffed config hashes: model weights hash matches prod float16 release; token merges identical.

Arjun: can you attach a minimal repro that shows truncation locally? If it's KV drift, we can repro with --max-new-tokens=200 and attach past KV states.

Mia: attached a short repro inline:
```
input = "TABLE:
Row1: id=1, amount=$1,234.56
Row2: id=2, amount=$2,345.67
Q: summarize amounts"
# iris-lora-v3 int4 -> output stops after Row1 amount (missing rest)
```

Devin: ok please run with `--log-kv=true --seed=42` and paste the first 3 kv entries around token 120-132. That will tell us whether caching is evicting early.

Mia: running now, will post when done.

eval-bot: QuickProbe started for model iris-lora-v3 (int4) by Mia at 1753334448. Job id qp-2026-03-21-07.

Mia: KV excerpt (trimmed):
```
kv[118] = <tok 5021: "$">
kv[119] = <tok 29: "1">
kv[120] = <tok 300: ",">
kv[121] = <tok 88: "234">
kv[122] = <tok 12: ".">
kv[123] = <tok 7: "56">
kv[124] = <tok 0: "\\n">
kv[125] = <tok 5021: "$">  # repeated, next row should follow but dp mismatch here
kv[126] = <tok 29: "2">
kv[127] = <tok 300: ",">
```

Mia: notice at kv[125] the dp (dot-product) is lower by ~0.12 vs float baseline. Could be quantization scale mismatch for the output head.

Arjun: that supports int4 scale mismatch. Two quick experiments: 1) run int4 with per-channel rescale (if supported) 2) run one step of bias-fix postquant (calibrated on small dataset). If either fixes, we pin a mitigation path.

Mia: I ran per-channel rescale enabled -> numeric-integrity moves to 0.95, pass 56/60, truncation resolves on repro. Looks promising.

Sara: nice. Any throughput hit? We need perf telemetry for customer SLA.

Mia: per-channel rescale adds ~4% latency on 1024 context bench. Still within their SLO.

Devin: two action items: 1) Arjun, can you add per-channel rescale as a recommended profile for iris-lora-v3 int4? 2) Mia, please re-run full quickpack and upload results to the PR. I'll flag the customer channel with a note that we recommend int4+per-channel rescale for now.

Arjun: will open a profile PR and add a small note in the model-catalog.

Mia: re-run kicked off qp-2026-03-21-07-full at 1753334480. I'll attach results.

OpsBot: Reminder: when shipping config changes to Dedicated clusters, file a change-request and include perf delta.

Devin: thanks everyone. If rescale holds on full run, we'll mark this as "int4-compatible with rescale" and ship a note to the Iris account.

Mia: thanks — will follow up with full pack and sample diffs. :thumbsup:
